title: Choose Clutch's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Repair Order. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Repair Order
options.lineage: numbered shop repair orders and multi-part carbon work forms
options.thesis: Every verified repair is a numbered work order, and each copy — Clutch, customer, employer — is a named source of proof.
options.viewport: Phone-first: the mechanic's record header as a filled form — photo attached, Identity and Screening as checked boxes, then a ruled ledger where 'Brakes 18 · BMW 6' is the loudest type, highlighted when the link carries your car.
options.risk: Rendered timidly it reads like paperwork; it only works if the rules, numerals and ink are executed with Stripe-level precision.

raised.raise: Unproven fields stay visible as designed blanks, never hidden — absence is drawn as carefully as proof.
One highlighter: only the lines matching the customer's car and repair get a single canary stroke.
Numerals carry the force: repair counts are the heaviest type on the page, tabular and ruled.
One owned ink: carbon blue belongs to verification alone and is never decorative.
One axis: the profile reads down a single form column; the eye path never branches.
The mechanic's photo is attached to the record like a real print, not cropped into a stock avatar circle.

options.label: The Vehicle History Report
options.lineage: vehicle history reports and inspection certificates
options.thesis: A mechanic's profile read like a history report: a summary verdict up top, then a dated event log with a source on every line.
options.viewport: Summary box of checks and counts, then a chronological log of verified repairs with source per row.
options.risk: Closest to Carfax itself — familiar and effective, and where most runs in this category would land.

options.label: Seven-Segment Display
options.thesis: Counts as lit segments on a dark panel.
options.viewport: Repair counts as big lit digits.
options.case: Loses both axes: reads as gas-station signage, not trust.
options.risk: Cheap-signage associations the brief rules out.
options.kept: Absence designed as deliberately as light.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine
options.thesis: Trust explained like a friend's doodle.
options.viewport: Marker headline and doodled arrows to badges.
options.case: Loses both axes: too casual for a serious hiring decision.
options.kept: One highlighter marking the line that matters.

options.label: Forge & Scale
options.lineage: blacksmith forging under a power hammer
options.case: Loses both axes: drifts toward the enthusiast/garage-grunge look the brief bans.
options.risk: Reads as a racing or tool brand.

options.label: Single-Hue Program
options.viewport: Full-bleed brand colour with a swept logotype.
options.case: Loses both axes: a flooded hue would drown the provenance distinctions.
options.risk: Toy-brand energy on a hiring decision.
options.kept: Total commitment to one owned colour.

options.label: Versailles Vistas
options.thesis: The profile as an axial garden walk.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link to the audience's world.
options.kept: A single axis the eye never leaves.

options.label: Tropicália Sleeve
options.thesis: Mechanics pasted into a crowded tableau.
options.case: Loses both axes: chaos where calm legibility is the job.
options.kept: Photography treated as real, physical material.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean marketplace profile — big photo, badges, stars, price and a blue button — executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Photo, name, star rating and badge row, with a booking card on the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Thumbtack or Airbnb by design.
